name: Hemadri Shekhar Das
bio: I completed an M.Sc. in Computer Science at Chennai Mathematical Institute in 2026, following a B.Sc. in Mathematics (Honours) from Asutosh College, University of Calcutta.

My current interests are in computer networks, particularly datacenter networking, congestion-aware routing, load balancing, and programmable networks. I have used network simulation and experimental analysis to investigate routing approaches and their performance under different traffic conditions.

Beyond networking, I'm interested in concurrent and systems programming, embedded systems, Linux, and self-hosted services. I enjoy understanding how software interacts with operating systems and hardware, and learning by building practical projects.

research.thesis: Load Balancing in Data Center Networks
research.current: Evaluating RTT-aware flowlet routing in ns-3.48

projects.name: rtt-aware-routing
projects.summary: An ns-3 implementation exploring RTT-aware flowlet routing as an alternative approach to datacenter load balancing. Evaluation against CONGA and ECMP is ongoing.
details: Implements several RTT-based path-selection policies using per-uplink EWMA estimates and TCP ACK feedback.
Compares algorithms on symmetric and asymmetric leaf-spine fabrics using shared traffic traces, payload accounting, and flow completion time analysis. Current RTT results are preliminary.
The prototype relies on TCP feedback. Transport-independent measurement for traffic such as RoCEv2 remains future work.

projects.name: RCR_Password_Manager
projects.summary: An implementation of the RCR 32/64 stream cipher within a password-manager coursework project. It was modelled after Bitwarden.
details: Implements cipher state, key/IV setup, and 32-bit and 64-bit keystream generation.
Supports PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and Argon2id for password-based key derivation, followed by HKDF-SHA256 for separate key material.
Processes file encryption and decryption in chunks, with HMAC-SHA256 authentication and tag comparison.

projects.name: Morse_Web_Controller_ESP32
projects.summary: A browser-controlled ESP32-C3 Morse transmitter, built to support maritime-signaling instruction for a Second Mate Officer course.
details: FreeRTOS tasks handle Morse generation, relay control, and Wi-Fi access-point connectivity.
Browser controls provide adjustable timing, start/stop/pause/resume, and separate test and main transmission stages.
Built for teaching the Second Mate Officer course. The public repository contains a subset of the project.

projects.name: Data_Mining_and_Machine_Learning_2025
projects.summary: Assignment notebooks from the Data Mining and Machine Learning course.

projects.name: trafpy
projects.summary: Adapted TrafPy to generate traffic workloads and support trace-based evaluation of datacenter load-balancing algorithms in ns-3.
details: Generated rack-aware and cross-rack workloads for early 100 Mb/s experiments, with CSV exports for ns-3.
Analysis notebooks match input and output flows and compare CONGA, ECMP, and RTT policies. Later 10 Gb/s experiments use a separate trace generator.
The original traffic generator and benchmark models are credited to TrafPy; local adaptations include plotting compatibility and removal of mandatory GPU initialization from selected paths.

projects.name: Networking_Fundamentals_2025
projects.summary: Course assignments and a presentation on networking fundamentals.

intro: I study how datacenter networks spread traffic across paths. My MSc thesis implemented CONGA in ns-3 and explored Power of Two Choices; that variant did not improve on CONGA.
I’m now evaluating smoothed RTT as a congestion signal for flowlet routing. Results are preliminary. Outside research, I build embedded projects and run a home lab.
